title: Core GDPR Compliance
description: Lawful basis for processing, data minimization, purpose limitation, transparency obligations, and data subject rights
key_actions: Identify and document lawful basis for each processing activity
Update privacy notices to cover new data processing
Conduct data mapping and create Records of Processing Activities (RoPA)
Implement data subject rights mechanisms (access, deletion, portability)
Review and update data retention schedules
deal_breaker_conditions: Cannot process personal data without a valid lawful basis. Launch impossible without at minimum: privacy notice, lawful basis documentation, and data subject rights process.
managed_risk_conditions: Full RoPA and DPIA may be completed post-launch if a preliminary assessment shows low risk and basic safeguards are in place.

regulation: GDPR Art. 35 — Data Protection Impact Assessment
title: DPIA Requirement
description: Mandatory DPIA for high-risk processing, including profiling, large-scale data processing, and systematic monitoring
key_actions: Conduct DPIA before starting the processing
Document necessity and proportionality of processing
Identify and assess risks to data subjects
Define mitigation measures for identified risks
Consult with DPO and, if required, with supervisory authority
deal_breaker_conditions: DPIA is legally required BEFORE processing begins. Cannot launch profiling-based services without completing DPIA first.

title: Automated Decision-Making Safeguards
description: Individuals have the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which significantly affect them
key_actions: Implement meaningful human oversight in decision-making process
Provide clear information to data subjects about automated decision logic
Implement right to contest automated decisions and obtain human review
Document that explicit consent or contractual necessity justifies automated decisions
Ensure the AI system can explain its output in understandable terms
deal_breaker_conditions: Cannot deploy fully automated decisions with significant effects on individuals without safeguards. Financial services (credit scoring) is explicitly highlighted in GDPR recitals.
managed_risk_conditions: If human reviewer is in the loop and decisions are advisory (not binding), Art. 22 may not be triggered — but robust documentation is needed.

regulation: GDPR Chapter V — International Data Transfers
title: Cross-Border Data Transfer Mechanisms
description: Transfers of personal data to third countries require adequate safeguards (SCCs, adequacy decisions, BCRs)
key_actions: Identify all international data flows and recipient countries
Conduct Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) for each transfer
Implement Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with data importers
Deploy supplementary technical measures (encryption, pseudonymization)
Document adequacy of protection in recipient country
deal_breaker_conditions: Cannot transfer EU personal data to US without valid transfer mechanism. Post-Schrems II, SCCs require supplementary measures for US transfers.
managed_risk_conditions: If EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification is in place for the US recipient, transfer is simplified — but verify certification status.

regulation: EU AI Act — High-Risk AI Systems
title: High-Risk AI System Requirements
description: AI systems in Annex III high-risk areas (employment, creditworthiness, essential services) face mandatory requirements including risk management, data governance, transparency, human oversight, and conformity assessment
key_actions: Classify the AI system under Annex III risk categories
Implement risk management system (Art. 9)
Ensure data governance and training data quality (Art. 10)
Create technical documentation (Art. 11)
Implement logging and traceability (Art. 12)
Provide transparency information to deployers (Art. 13)
Design for human oversight (Art. 14)
Ensure accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity (Art. 15)
Conduct conformity assessment before placing on market
deal_breaker_conditions: AI systems used for credit scoring or employment decisions are classified as high-risk under Annex III. Full compliance is required before market placement. Fines up to EUR 35M or 7% of global turnover.
managed_risk_conditions: If the AI system is purely advisory (no automated decisions) and the deployer implements human oversight, some requirements may be lighter — but classification as high-risk still requires full documentation.

regulation: EU AI Act — General-Purpose AI / Transparency
title: General AI Transparency Obligations
description: All AI systems must meet basic transparency requirements; general-purpose AI models have additional obligations
key_actions: Ensure AI system is clearly identified as AI to users
Document the AI system's intended purpose and limitations
Provide deployers with instructions for use
Implement content marking where applicable (AI-generated content)
managed_risk_conditions: Basic transparency requirements can often be met through documentation and UI labeling. Lower risk if system is B2B and deployers are informed.

title: Cookie Consent and Electronic Communications
description: Consent required for non-essential cookies and tracking technologies; specific rules for electronic marketing communications
key_actions: Implement cookie consent banner for analytics/tracking cookies
Document cookie categories and purposes
Ensure marketing emails comply with opt-in requirements
Provide easy opt-out mechanism
managed_risk_conditions: If the product is B2B SaaS without direct consumer tracking, ePrivacy obligations are limited. Focus on any analytics or monitoring features.

title: ESG Reporting Compliance
description: Large and listed EU companies must report on sustainability using European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). From 2026, mid-market companies (250+ employees) are also in scope.
key_actions: Ensure the reporting module covers all mandatory ESRS disclosure areas
Implement data quality controls for sustainability metrics
Support double materiality assessment workflow
Provide audit trail for reported metrics
Align output formats with XBRL tagging requirements
managed_risk_conditions: As a tool provider (not a reporting entity), TechForward's main risk is accuracy of the tool's guidance and calculations. Incorrect reporting templates could expose clients and create liability.

title: EU Taxonomy Alignment
description: Classification system for environmentally sustainable economic activities. Companies in scope of CSRD must report Taxonomy-aligned revenue, CapEx, and OpEx.
key_actions: Include Taxonomy eligibility and alignment assessment in the reporting module
Map client activities to Taxonomy-defined economic activities
Implement Technical Screening Criteria checks
Support Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) assessment
Include minimum social safeguards verification
managed_risk_conditions: Taxonomy reporting is mandatory for CSRD-scoped companies. The tool should correctly implement screening criteria to avoid client misreporting.

regulation: BaFin — AI in Financial Services Guidance
title: BaFin Supervisory Requirements for AI
description: BaFin expects regulated entities using AI for risk assessment or customer-facing decisions to ensure explainability, auditability, and non-discrimination. Supervisory guidance applies to banks, insurers, and their service providers.
key_actions: Ensure AI model is explainable to BaFin-regulated deployers
Implement model validation and backtesting framework
Document model governance including change management
Conduct bias and discrimination testing
Provide audit trail of model decisions and inputs
Align with MaRisk (Minimum Requirements for Risk Management) for IT
deal_breaker_conditions: Banking clients cannot deploy AI risk scoring without meeting BaFin expectations. If TechForward's product doesn't support the required explainability and auditability, banks cannot use it.
managed_risk_conditions: If the AI output is advisory only and the bank implements its own model governance wrapper, some requirements may be met by the deployer rather than TechForward.

regulation: CCPA/CPRA (California Consumer Privacy Act / California Privacy Rights Act)
title: California Privacy Compliance
description: California residents have rights to know, delete, and opt out of sale/sharing of personal information. Additional protections for sensitive personal information and automated decision-making.
key_actions: Update privacy policy for CCPA/CPRA disclosures
Implement 'Do Not Sell or Share' opt-out mechanism
Honor consumer rights requests (access, deletion, correction)
Classify personal information categories per CPRA requirements
Implement opt-in for sensitive personal information use
Conduct privacy risk assessment for automated decision-making
managed_risk_conditions: For B2B services processing employee data, CPRA's service provider provisions apply. Contractual agreements with clients can address most requirements.

regulation: US State Privacy Laws (Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, etc.)
title: Multi-State US Privacy Compliance
description: Multiple US states have enacted comprehensive privacy laws with varying requirements for data processing, consumer rights, and automated decision-making.
key_actions: Map which state laws apply based on user/data subject locations
Implement a unified privacy rights mechanism covering all applicable states
Conduct data protection assessments where required
Review contracts with US clients for state-specific provisions
managed_risk_conditions: Most US state laws have B2B exemptions or service provider safe harbors. Focus compliance on employee data processing, which is less exempted.

title: Employee Data Processing — EU Framework
description: Processing employee data is subject to GDPR plus national employment data protection laws (e.g., § 26 BDSG in Germany). Works council co-determination may apply for monitoring tools.
key_actions: Identify lawful basis for employee data processing (consent is problematic in employment context)
Assess whether works council co-determination applies (§ 87 Abs. 1 Nr. 6 BetrVG)
Ensure data minimization — only process data necessary for the stated purpose
Conduct DPIA for employee profiling or performance analytics
Provide employee transparency notices
Address national variations (Germany: § 26 BDSG; France: CNIL guidance; Netherlands: UAVG)
deal_breaker_conditions: Employee performance profiling and attrition prediction are highly sensitive. In Germany, works council involvement is required before deployment. Without it, the product cannot be used by German clients.
managed_risk_conditions: If the product provides anonymized/aggregated insights only (no individual profiling), employment data protection obligations are significantly reduced.

regulation: US Anti-Discrimination Laws (Title VII, ADEA, ADA) and NYC Local Law 144
title: AI Bias and Employment Discrimination
description: AI tools used in employment decisions must not result in disparate impact on protected classes. NYC Local Law 144 requires annual bias audits for automated employment decision tools.
key_actions: Conduct disparate impact analysis across protected classes (race, gender, age, disability)
Implement annual bias audit (required for NYC-based clients under LL144)
Publish bias audit results summary and provide notice to candidates/employees
Document validation study showing the AI tool is job-related and consistent with business necessity
Implement ongoing monitoring for bias drift
deal_breaker_conditions: If TechForward's AI model shows disparate impact and cannot demonstrate business necessity, US clients face significant litigation risk. NYC clients cannot deploy without a published bias audit.
managed_risk_conditions: If the tool provides analytics/insights only and does not make or directly influence specific employment decisions, the obligations are reduced but not eliminated.
